intuition.title: Separate well thickness from well count
intuition.summary: System II increases the thickness of one HgS well; system III places an additional HgS well across a CdS barrier. Comparing these with system I probes how spatial separation changes carrier confinement and optical transitions. The actual paper tests one stated barrier thickness, rather than a systematic barrier-thickness series.

intuition.title: pH-mediated nucleation and growth
intuition.summary: The authors propose that high initial pH rapidly ionizes H₂S, enabling many small CdS nuclei. Continued dissociation and precipitation release acidity, slow further growth and lead to the final acidic pH. The printed sulfur-ion notation is S⁻; it is retained as source wording rather than treated as a validated solution-speciation measurement.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
